title: Accuracy of chronic kidney disease codes against laboratory-defined disease in six general practices: a diagnostic accuracy study using existing records
abstract: Objective: to estimate the sensitivity and positive predictive value of kidney disease stage 3 to 5 codes against laboratory-defined disease. Design: cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study of pseudonymised records of adults registered with six practices, with a random review of 200 discordant records. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Kidney disease codes drive reviews and medicine safety checks in general practice, but they may miss patients with persistently low eGFR and may label patients after a single low result. A recorded literature search returned no records for this question.
methods: Adults with at least two eGFR results between January 2019 and June 2026 were classified by code and by laboratory results (two values below 60 at least 90 days apart). Sensitivity and positive predictive value were estimated with Wilson intervals; adults tested once were reported separately.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the flow of adults, the two-by-two table, accuracy estimates overall and by subgroup, and reasons for discordance.
discussion: The discussion will interpret accuracy against the recoding decision, weigh partial verification, and compare the estimates with published studies once they have been retrieved and checked.
limitations: Partial verification; one laboratory; codes as the only record of diagnosis; six practices in one network.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will be limited to coding accuracy in these practices.
summary: STARD-structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
